body: Hokum far exceeded my expectations, and that comes from someone who enjoyed his previous movie Oddity. Hokum is rich with atmosphere, tension, and delivers on scares. While not an entirely unique premise, Hokum achieves where other similar titles flounder. Characters are rich, the film is effortlessly funny without being annoying, and the scares are plentiful. I think this film will be a new classic people reach for every Halloween season.

I watched an early screening of this film and wow was I blown away! I love horror films and don't scare that easily, but this film got me squirming in my seat for nearly the entire runtime! I was fighting to stay in my own seat because of how terrifying some of the visuals were! The way this film plays with sound, light, and cramped spaces is what truly brings the horror of this film to life! I loved every second of it and I highly recommend it be seen in theaters by anyone who loves getting scared! It will keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish and will stick with you for a while after! One of the best original horror films of the year so far!

If I am ever being chased by witches, I won't draw a circle I'll look for a psychiatrist

Ohm Bauman heads to Ireland to scatter his parents ashes. He stays in a hotel in the woods that his parents had their honeymoon in. He immediately met with some Irish folklore. When a member of staff goes missing there is only one room locked away in the Hotel that hasn't been searched, the honeymoon suite. Locked for a good reason, the room is rumoured to be occupied by a witch.

I really enjoyed this film. It's funny, it has a very good story, good mystery, and good jumpscares. The movie shines when it uses the shadows opposed to jumpscares to deliver the fright. The effects are good and so is the pacing.

A very tense movie that around the 20 minute mark things kick off till the end. Adam Scott is a great lead, all the Hotel staff are also very good at acting and a shout to David Wilmot who plays Jerry, the man in the woods with a draw to the hotel.

I would have liked a bit more on the Folklore side of things, the mystery is actually at the centre which is really good but I feel if we had more in the woods at night or more witch activity to lean into would be cool.

Some questions remaining at the end, surrounding the owner, was he aware of the dark secrets this hotel had, I'm not sure.

None the less, really good watch would see myself watching again, 8/10.

I'm not one to easily exaggerate, but I definitely think that this is one of the scariest movies that I've ever seen.

Director Damien McCarthy made an incredibly effective horror film. One that genuinely made me scared to drive home alone at night. Which is honestly the best compliment that I can give a horror movie.

But Adam Scott does an excellent job of leading this well-made film.

Hokum is not only one of the best horror movies of the year, it's also currently one of my favorite films of the year. Period.

Hokum plays with the horror genre in ways that are a little different than most horror films. I really liked that.

The film has many of the same elements of a horror film with supernatural events and beings. There are the scares and eerie feelings that we have become accustomed to in stories like these. It does a good job of dealing with the normal horror.

What i was not expecting was a mystery at the same time. A who done it that elevates the material significantly. This wss my favorite part of the film.

Adam Scott is exceptional as our protagonist. He plays a depressed, unlikable type of fellow who falls in to this mystery and has to be inventive to find his way out. It's fun to watch.

Overall a good time at the movies for any horror fan.
